question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=2 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-3$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-3) &=-7 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-16 \\ {x}_{1} &=8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=8$ and ${x}_{2}=-3$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=9 \\ 3(8)+5(-3) &=9 \\ 9 &=9\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=8$ and ${x}_{2}=-3$, which means

$$
8{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(8)+(-3)=5.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -4 \\ 14\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -4 \\ 14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -4 \\ 14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -4 \\ 14\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-8 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-4 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-12 \\ {x}_{2} &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=6$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-8 \\ {x}_{1}-(6) &=-8 \\ {x}_{1} &=-2 \\ {x}_{1} &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=6$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=14 \\ 2(-2)+3(6) &=14 \\ 14 &=14\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=6$, which means

$$
-2{a}_{1}+6{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+(6)=4.
$$

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the first equation we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{1} & =7-4 \\ {x}_{1} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now,  we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ into the third equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} & =4 \\ 3(3)-{x}_{2} & =4 \\ -{x}_{2} & =4-9 \\ {x}_{2} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the second equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =9 \\ -2(3)+3(5) & =9 \\ -6+15 & =9,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5,$ which means

$$
3{a}_{1}+5{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+5=8.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=5 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$, which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =3 \\ -{x}_{1}+2 & =3 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =5 \\ -(-1)+2(2) & =5 \\ 5 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ 10 \\ -20\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=24 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=10 \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-20\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$, the second equation by $2$, and adding the resulting equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}23{x}_{2} &=92 \\ {x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=10 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4(4) &=10 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=-6 \\ {x}_{1} &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-20 \\ 4(-2)-3(4) &=-20 \\ -20 &=-20\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=4$, which means

$$
-2{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+(4)=2.
$$
